items.stem: Motion between two keyframes looks mechanical. Which adjustment most directly makes it feel natural?

options.text: Apply easing / adjust the velocity curve in the graph editor
options.rationale: Correct: easing and velocity curves shape acceleration for natural motion.

options.text: Increase the composition frame rate only
options.rationale: Frame rate affects smoothness of playback, not the easing feel between keyframes.
More linear keyframes keep motion mechanical.

options.text: Enable motion blur on an unrelated layer
options.rationale: Motion blur on another layer does not change this motion's timing.

items.explanation: Correct: easing and velocity curves shape acceleration for natural motion.

items.stem: Why would you precompose a group of layers?

options.text: To treat them as a single layer for ordering, effects and reuse
options.rationale: Correct: precomposing nests layers so they can be managed and effected together.

options.text: To permanently flatten and delete the source layers
options.rationale: Precomposing nests layers; it does not delete the originals.

options.text: To change the project colour depth
options.rationale: Colour depth is a project setting, unrelated to precomposing.

options.text: To export directly to social media
options.rationale: Precomposing is an organisation step, not an export action.

items.explanation: Correct: precomposing nests layers so they can be managed and effected together.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid reasons to use an adjustment layer?

options.text: Apply an effect to all layers beneath it
options.rationale: Correct: an adjustment layer affects layers below it in the stack.

options.text: Apply a consistent colour look across multiple layers at once
options.rationale: Correct: one adjustment layer can grade everything beneath it.
Adjustment layers do not store rendered output.

options.text: Replace the need for a composition
options.rationale: An adjustment layer lives inside a composition; it does not replace one.

items.explanation: Correct: an adjustment layer affects layers below it in the stack.
